findings.claim: Estimates are commitments under social pressure, not predictions. ... should treat the underlying estimates as commitments under social pressure with large intrinsic variation.

findings.claim: the two exponentials being driven by the two independent processes ... For reliability investment decisions, this means a small set of inputs drives most fault experiences — the right investment is in shaping the input profile ...
findings.failure_mode: Jones's explicitly 'speculative' explanation is stated as fact, and the ranked-duplicate-fault curve is re-read as 'a small set of inputs drives most fault experiences'. The investment rule is the distillation's synthesis. It is partly backed by deep 159 (reliability research neglects input distributions) and 171 (fixing all mistakes is wasted), but it is presented as what the pattern 'means'.
findings.fix: correct: ... Jones speculates the two exponentials reflect two interacting processes: input-value distribution and source-code mistakes. For reliability investment, it suggests a few faults are experienced far more often than the rest, so profiling repeat fault experiences before budgeting is worth more than pursuing comprehensive defect-free code.

findings.claim: **KLOC, Halstead, and McCabe are folklore metrics.**

notes: Quotations checked in source: 'can be easily manipulated by splitting functions with high values into two or more functions, each having lower metric values' (24220-24222), 'accounting fraud' (24286-24287), 'gave birth to this demon meme', 'how not to do it', DoD-Std-2167 clause (21375-21380): all verbatim. Deep-ref issues surfaced for cycling: (1) deep 103's Bass peak formula fuses peak sales and peak time (source 17532-17540); (2) deep 91 says real options is presented with warnings of inapplicability, but the source warns only against Black-Scholes. Questions that reuse an already-flagged premise (incumbent-vendor 'moat' at lines 67, 298; bi-exponential 'high-frequency peak' at lines 78, 110, 114, 165, 225) are counted as faithful applied guidance, with the premise graded once at its Key Concept. The worked example attributes a fabricated '9:1' claim to a McKinsey deck; this is hypothetical but names a real firm, so worth softening to 'a consultancy deck'. Runtime-trigger rows paraphrase rather than lift the task-spec trigger text (dropped parentheticals, 'for software work'), and 'openstax-*-software-business (pending)' labels are stale (those files exist); neither is a source-fidelity issue. '1:10:100 cost-of-fix' is used as a folklore label the deep ref never names; the correction attributed to Jones (NASA/DOD hardware-cost context) is supported. Integration rows for Accounting Vol 2, Principles of Management and Principles of Marketing check out.
